summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled 'Book 10 — part 64') in which Patricia and her date Damian are at a beach where a surfer drowns after the undertow pulls two surfers out to sea. Patricia, who is dizzy and has been caught in a mishap, is helped by Damian, and she performs CPR on the surfer until paramedics take over. Damian tells her he loves her, and the two drive home late through LA, where parts of the city are on fire and traffic is slow.
one_line: Patricia and Damian's beach date ends in a surfer's death and a late, slow drive home through a burning Los Angeles.
key_facts: Patricia asks Damian to get her to the sea so she can soak her head, and he walks her into the water still in his suit-pants, dress shirt and tie.
Damian points to a Coast Guard clipper zooming toward the shore and says he fired up a couple flares because the cell-phone was dead.
Patricia does airway-breathing-circulation checks on the surfer, finds no pulse, and begins CPR by slamming him onto his back.
Two paramedics take over working on the surfer, and someone puts a robe over Patricia's shoulders and a cup of juice in her hands.
Patricia realizes she hasn't depilated in a week and had spent a crucial amount of time naked in front of her date's family.
Damian kisses Patricia and says, "I love you, Patricia," and she responds, "Ooh... You're breaking the rules!"
Patricia says, "Just don't make a habit of it, you lunk."
The surfer dies, which spoils what would otherwise have been a perfect evening.
Patricia and Damian do not get home until well after midnight.
Parts of LA appear to be on fire as they inch along the freeway.
The couple is used to driving 60 or 70 on the freeway, and over 80 if traffic is light.
The year before, the New Yorker ran a 40-page paean to LA, calling it the most livable city in America now that it had licked its traffic problems.
